newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends down vs dlr on import cover.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends down vs dlr on import cover.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed weaker against the dollar at 57.16 on Monday after demand for the greenback emerged to cover imports, dealers said.

"The market closed around the central bank selling level," said a foreign bank dealer. "In the morning one or two banks sold and spot came down to 57.03. Then a foreign bank came in and bought and the dollar went up to 57.16."
The Central Bank kept buying and selling levels unchanged at 56.0266 and 57.1584 despite its strength overseas prompting some dealers to speculate it will push the dollar up on Tuesday.
"The central bank could put the dollar up by three or four cents tomorrow because overseas the dollar has strengthened," said a state bank dealer.
The rupee opened firmer at 57.02 because of high rupee interest rates but fell when banks bought dollars to cover imports or short positions, dealers said.
Overnight call money rates closed around 19 percent as both state banks were borrowing heavily, dealers said.
